papers.title: Meta-Analysis of Face-Validity Indicators in Automatically Detected Dog Sleep Spindles.
papers.summary: The authors evaluated their automatic dog sleep spindle detector against three face-validity criteria from human EEG (duration, midline distribution, amplitude-chirp association) across many datasets. Most datasets satisfied all criteria, supporting the detector's quality and the dog as a model.

papers.title: Characterizing transition state in mouse vigilance with electroencephalogram-electromyogram hypnodensity.
papers.summary: The authors characterized mouse vigilance-state transition dynamics using EEG/EMG and expert annotations, finding that NREMS-to-REMS transitions are longest and REMS-to-NREMS shortest. SVM classifiers trained on stable-state features successfully predicted transition midpoints, providing a reproducible framework.

papers.title: Diurnal time and sleep pressure modulate cerebrospinal fluid low-frequency oscillations in synchrony with wake-promoting nuclei
papers.summary: In a 34-hour sleep deprivation study, CSF low-frequency oscillations (vasomotion) increased with time awake and peaked in the early morning, correlating with vigilance and reticular activating system activity, but not with EEG slow waves or norepinephrine. This suggests wake-promoting nuclei drive vasomotion.

papers.title: Fully-automated sleep staging for Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: The authors finetuned the U-Sleep deep neural network for automated sleep staging in Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder, improving Cohen's kappa from 0.66 to 0.74 after finetuning. Confidence thresholds enhanced REM precision to 95.6%, achieving human-level agreement.

papers.title: REM Sleep Disengagement of β Oscillations Permits Rapid Dream Movements in Parkinsonism
papers.summary: In MPTP-treated non-human primates, pathological beta oscillations and motor impairments were attenuated during REM sleep, with beta suppression preceding REM onset. This indicates that parkinsonian network dysfunction is dynamically gated by brain state, revealing latent capacity for rapid movement during REM.

papers.title: A Novel Adversarial Approach for EEG Dataset Refinement: Enhancing Generalization Through Proximity-to-Boundary Scoring.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a training framework using a proximity-to-boundary score to reduce the influence of noisy EEG samples, improving model generalization by 1.43-6.66% on motor imagery and 0.72-2.85% on sleep stage datasets without extra hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Leednet: a lightweight network for event detection in EEG signals.
papers.summary: This paper introduces LEEDNet, a lightweight convolutional network for classifying short EEG events (normal, slow waves, spike/sharp waves), achieving 81.2% accuracy and 77.5% macro-F1 on the NMT-Events dataset with 0.25M parameters and <5 ms inference on CPU.

papers.title: Chronic corticosterone exposure disrupts bile acids homeostasis associated with circadian dysfunction in the liver of chickens.
papers.summary: This study shows chronic corticosterone exposure disrupts hepatic circadian clock and bile acid homeostasis in chickens, altering clock gene rhythms and bile acid levels, with dexamethasone promoting MRP2-mediated bile acid efflux in vitro.

papers.title: An EEG-based fatigue detection framework integrating interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling.
papers.summary: This paper presents AXELLSTM, an EEG-based fatigue detection framework with interpretable feature and channel selection, achieving 0.7454 accuracy and 0.7143 macro-F1 in cross-subject LOSO validation while being computationally efficient.

papers.title: Epi-Spec2State: Convolutional state space model via spectrogram image sequences for prediction-oriented seizure state classification in EEG signals.
papers.summary: This paper proposes Epi-Spec2State, a convolutional state space model using spectrogram image sequences for seizure state classification, achieving 96.40-96.60% accuracy on clinical SEEG data and outperforming nine SOTA methods on public datasets.

papers.title: Automated autism spectrum disorder detection using EEG signals and time-frequency visibility graphs.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a dual-domain framework for automated ASD detection using EEG signals, integrating time-frequency analysis with Horizontal Visibility Graph-based network modeling. The DWT-HVG approach with a Soft Voting Ensemble achieved 93.54% accuracy and 98.17% AUC, demonstrating an accurate and interpretable method for objective ASD screening.

papers.title: Aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia on the jaw muscle electromyographic activities during sleep in young adult rats.
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) on jaw muscle activity during sleep in young adult rats, finding that CIH increased FosB expression in brainstem regions and noradrenergic fiber density in the trigeminal motor nucleus, and selectively enhanced digastric muscle activity during arousal from sleep, without altering overall sleep structure.

papers.title: A Multi-Scale Adaptive EEG Feature Selection and Weighting Method for Mental Workload Estimation in Rapid Serial Visual Presentation.
papers.summary: This paper introduced a Multi-scale Adaptive Feature selection and Augmented Weighting (MAFA) framework for mental workload estimation in RSVP-BCIs, using adaptive channel selection and multi-scale feature weighting. The method achieved higher classification accuracy than comparison approaches and revealed posterior theta and alpha band features, supporting its feasibility and interpretability.

papers.title: Acute sleep deprivation rank-dependently enhances offensive aggression via the PVN in male mice.
papers.summary: Investigating the effects of acute sleep deprivation (ASD) on aggression in male mice, this study found that ASD selectively enhanced offensive aggression in dominant but not subordinate mice, via increased PVN activation, and chemogenetic inhibition of PVN neurons reversed this effect, revealing a critical interaction between sleep loss and social hierarchy.

papers.title: Respiratory phase shapes brain-heart dynamics: evidence from recurrence analysis of EEG band power and heart rate.
papers.summary: This study examined respiratory-phase-dependent modulation of brain-heart interactions during controlled breathing, finding that inhale-hold increased gamma power, recurrence rate, and heart rate, while exhale-hold reduced them, suggesting distinct dynamical regimes and supporting respiration as a modulator of brain-body dynamics.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment attenuates chronic stress-induced disruptions in the gut microbiota, intestinal barrier, and brain.
papers.summary: In a chronic unpredictable mild stress mouse model, environmental enrichment reduced depressive-like behavior, restored hippocampal and raphe markers, and prevented stress-induced gut microbiota alterations and intestinal barrier disruption, suggesting it stabilizes the microbiota-gut-brain axis.

papers.title: Sleep and psychosis: An integrative review of conceptual and neurophysiological associations.
papers.summary: This integrative review summarizes conceptual and neurophysiological associations between sleep processes and psychosis, noting limited direct neurobiological evidence but potential overlap in anterior cingulate and frontal regions, and highlights gaps for future research.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture improves neurocognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation: an experimental study based on hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity.
papers.summary: In rats, electro-nape-acupuncture at GB20 and Gongxue improved cognitive deficits induced by chronic sleep deprivation by restoring hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity in the dentate gyrus, suggesting a potential therapy for cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Associations of Plasma Total Tau Level and MMSE Score With Polysomnographic Data in Middle-Aged Men With Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: In middle-aged men with severe obstructive sleep apnea, plasma total tau levels correlated negatively with deep sleep duration and mean oxygen saturation, and positively with apnea-hypopnea index, oxygen desaturation index, and arousal index, while MMSE scores showed inverse correlations, linking intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation to neurodegeneration markers.

papers.title: Armillariella tabescens polysaccharide targets microglial glycolysis to alleviate sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation through the mTOR signaling pathway.
papers.summary: A polysaccharide from Armillariella tabescens (ATEP) alleviated sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits in mice by inhibiting mTOR signaling, which corrected glycolytic reprogramming and promoted microglial M2 polarization, highlighting its potential as a neuroprotective agent.

papers.title: Nocturnal heart rate variability in Parkinson's disease: associations with autonomic dysfunction, cognitive function, and mood symptoms.
papers.summary: This study compared nocturnal heart rate variability (HRV) between Parkinson's disease (PD) patients and healthy controls, finding reduced sympathetic influence in PD. In PD patients, stronger parasympathetic influence was associated with better cognitive performance, while subjective autonomic symptoms correlated with poorer cognition and mood.

papers.title: DTI-ALPS as a marker of glymphatic function: Review of the literature findings, methodology, and interpretation.
papers.summary: This review of 393 DTI-ALPS articles summarizes its use as a non-invasive MRI biomarker of glymphatic system function, with most studies finding significant associations with disease severity. However, the index is a sensitive but non-specific marker of white matter microstructural damage and neuroinflammation, with methodological variations affecting interpretation.

papers.title: Adolescent depression recognition and symptom prediction based on multi-view EEG network: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study developed a Multi-view Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (MVA-GCN) using resting-state EEG to classify adolescent depression, achieving 99.84% accuracy compared to 86.43% for questionnaire-based models. Occipital and fronto-central regions, increased gamma-band connectivity, and reduced alpha power were implicated, but brain-resilience correlations were not significant after correction.

papers.title: Physiologic and symptomatic burden across sleep-disordered breathing severity in men and women.
papers.summary: This community-based study examined sex differences in physiologic and symptomatic burden across sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) severity. Men showed greater sleep disruption and daytime sleepiness at moderate-to-severe SDB, while women had more insomnia symptoms and lower quality of life, indicating that SDB assessment should consider sex-specific impacts beyond AHI.

papers.title: Transcranial direct current stimulation enhances cognitive performance and modulates QEEG beta- and theta-band power in patients undergoing whole-brain radiotherapy.
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled study assessed tDCS in patients undergoing whole-brain radiotherapy, finding significant improvements in working memory and sustained attention with active stimulation. tDCS also reduced beta and theta EEG power and attenuated stress-related protein expression, supporting its potential as an adjunctive cognitive-preserving therapy.
